subject: System Design
title: How B-Trees Work
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: How B-Trees Work.

hook.text: A B-tree finds any row among a billion in about 30 disk reads. It's the backbone of most database indexes.

buildup.text: A B-tree is a balanced tree where each node holds multiple keys and pointers, organized for disk access.

discovery.text: Each level of the tree eliminates a branching factor of possibilities. With factor 500, 3 levels covers billions.

twist.text: B-trees must rebalance on inserts and deletes. Random writes cause fragmentation that slows performance.

climax.text: B-trees have been the dominant index structure since 1972. After 50 years, nothing has replaced them.

punchline.text: 50 years old and still the king of database indexes.

quiz.question: Why are B-trees efficient for databases?
options: Each level eliminates many possibilities, requiring few disk reads
They store data in memory only
